regimens.indication: NYHA Class III-IV Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (Adults)

refs.quote: In patients with serum potassium ≤5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >50 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , initiate treatment at 25 mg once daily. Patients who tolerate 25 mg once daily may have their dosage increased to 50 mg once daily as clinically indicated.

regimens.dose_text: Initiate at 25 mg orally once daily (if K+ <= 5.0 mEq/L and eGFR > 50 mL/min/1.73 m2); may increase to 50 mg once daily. For eGFR 30-50 mL/min/1.73 m2, consider initiating at 25 mg every other day. Reduce to 25 mg every other day if hyperkalemia develops.

refs.quote: The recommended initial daily dose is 25 to 100 mg of ALDACTONE administered in either single or divided doses is recommended. Dosage can be titrated at two-week intervals. Doses greater than 100 mg/day generally do not provide additional reductions in blood pressure.

dose.frequency: daily in single or divided doses

regimens.dose_text: 25 to 100 mg orally daily in single or divided doses; titrate at two-week intervals. Doses > 100 mg/day generally do not provide additional BP reduction.

regimens.indication: Edema Associated with Hepatic Cirrhosis or Nephrotic Syndrome (Adults)

refs.quote: In patients with cirrhosis, initiate therapy in a hospital setting and titrate slowly [see Use in Specific Populations (8.7) ] . The recommended initial daily dosage is 100 mg of ALDACTONE administered in either single or divided doses, but may range from 25 to 200 mg daily.

dose.frequency: daily in single or divided doses

regimens.dose_text: Initial daily dosage: 100 mg orally in single or divided doses (range 25 to 200 mg daily); initiate in a hospital setting and titrate slowly in patients with cirrhosis. Administer for at least 5 days before increasing dose when used as sole diuretic.

refs.quote: Administer ALDACTONE in doses of 100 to 400 mg daily in preparation for surgery.

regimens.dose_text: 100 to 400 mg orally daily in preparation for surgery.

regimens.indication: Primary Hyperaldosteronism - Long-Term Maintenance (Adults Unsuitable for Surgery)

refs.quote: For patients who are considered unsuitable for surgery, ALDACTONE can be used as long-term maintenance therapy at the lowest effective dosage determined for the individual patient.

regimens.dose_text: Use the lowest effective dosage determined for the individual patient.

ALDACTONE is substantially excreted by the kidney, and the risk of adverse reactions to this drug may be greater in patients with impaired renal function. Patients with renal impairment are at increased risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium closely.

hepatic.value: In patients with cirrhosis and ascites, initiate in the hospital with the lowest initial dose and titrate slowly; sudden fluid/electrolyte shifts may precipitate impaired neurological function, worsening hepatic encephalopathy, and coma.

refs.quote: ALDACTONE can cause sudden alterations of fluid and electrolyte balance which may precipitate impaired neurological function, worsening hepatic encephalopathy and coma in patients with hepatic disease with cirrhosis and ascites. In these patients, initiate ALDACTONE in the hospital

mg_safety.note: Can cause hyperkalemia and hyponatremia; monitor electrolytes in myasthenia gravis patients.

value.instructions: ALDACTONE film-coated immediate-release tablets (25 mg, 50 mg, 100 mg) may be crushed if needed; label does not specify dedicated NG tube instructions.

Metabolism: Hyperkalemia, electrolyte disturbances [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1 , 5.3) ] , hyponatremia, hypovolemia. Musculoskeletal: Leg cramps. Nervous system/psychiatric: Lethargy, mental confusion, ataxia, dizziness, headache, drowsiness.

Liver/biliary: A very few cases of mixed cholestatic/hepatocellular toxicity, with one reported fatality, have been reported with spironolactone administration. Renal: Renal dysfunction (including renal failure). Skin: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), alopecia, pruritis.

mechanism_of_action.value: Spironolactone and its active metabolites are specific pharmacologic antagonists of aldosterone, acting primarily through competitive binding of receptors at the aldosterone-dependent sodium-potassium exchange site in the distal convoluted renal tubule, increasing sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium.

refs.quote: Spironolactone and its active metabolites are specific pharmacologic antagonists of aldosterone, acting primarily through competitive binding of receptors at the aldosterone-dependent sodium-potassium exchange site in the distal convoluted renal tubule.

Spironolactone is rapidly and extensively metabolized. Metabolites can be divided into two main categories: those in which sulfur of the parent molecule is removed (e.g., canrenone) and those in which the sulfur is retained

value.effect: Concomitant use of eplerenone with spironolactone is contraindicated due to additive hyperkalemia risk.
value.management: Contraindicated; do not co-administer with eplerenone.

refs.quote: ALDACTONE is contraindicated in the patients with: • Hyperkalemia • Addison's disease • Concomitant use of eplerenone

value.management: Avoid concomitant use of ALDACTONE and mitotane.

value.drug_or_class: Drugs and Supplements Increasing Serum Potassium (ACEi, ARBs, NSAIDs, heparin/LMWH, trimethoprim, K+ supplements)
value.effect: Concomitant administration may lead to severe hyperkalemia.
value.management: In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients starting ALDACTONE; check serum potassium when ACEi or ARB therapy is altered.

refs.locator: Section 7.1 Drugs and Supplements Increasing Serum Potassium
refs.quote: Concomitant administration of ALDACTONE with potassium supplementation or drugs that can increase potassium may lead to severe hyperkalemia. In general, discontinue potassium supplementation in heart failure patients who start ALDACTONE

value.effect: Reduces renal clearance of lithium, increasing the risk of lithium toxicity.
value.management: Monitor lithium levels periodically when ALDACTONE is coadministered.

refs.quote: Like other diuretics, ALDACTONE reduces the renal clearance of lithium, thus increasing the risk of lithium toxicity. Monitor lithium levels periodically when ALDACTONE is coadministered

value.effect: Hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis has been reported with concurrent use.
value.management: Monitor electrolytes and acid-base status if co-administered.

refs.quote: Hyperkalemic metabolic acidosis has been reported in patients given ALDACTONE concurrently with cholestyramine.

value.effect: NSAIDs and ASA may reduce the diuretic, natriuretic, and antihypertensive efficacy of spironolactone.
value.management: Monitor closely for desired diuretic/antihypertensive effect; higher maintenance doses of ALDACTONE may be needed with ASA.

refs.quote: In some patients, the administration of an NSAID can reduce the diuretic, natriuretic, and antihypertensive effect of diuretics. Therefore, when ALDACTONE and NSAIDs are used concomitantly, monitor closely to determine if the desired effect of the diuretic is obtained

value.effect: Spironolactone and its metabolites interfere with radioimmunoassays for digoxin, increasing apparent digoxin exposure.
value.management: Use a digoxin assay that does not interact with spironolactone.

refs.quote: Spironolactone and its metabolites interfere with radioimmunoassays for digoxin and increase the apparent exposure to digoxin. It is unknown to what extent, if any, spironolactone may increase actual digoxin exposure. In patients taking concomitant digoxin, use an assay that does not interact with spironolactone.

value.effect: Spironolactone binds to the androgen receptor and may increase PSA levels in abiraterone-treated prostate cancer patients.
value.management: Concomitant use of spironolactone and abiraterone is not recommended.

refs.quote: Spironolactone binds to the androgen receptor and may increase prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels in abiraterone-treated prostate cancer patients. Concomitant use of spironolactone and abiraterone is not recommended.
Agents increasing serum potassium: Concomitant administration can lead to hyperkalemia ( 5.1 , 7.1 ). • Lithium: Increased risk of lithium toxicity ( 7.2 ).

Because of the potential risk to the male fetus due to anti-androgenic properties of spironolactone and animal data, avoid spironolactone in pregnant women or advise a pregnant woman of the potential risk to a male fetus.

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Label explicitly recommends avoiding spironolactone in pregnant women due to anti-androgenic properties; rat embryofetal studies demonstrated feminization of male fetuses and persistent endocrine dysfunction in offspring.

contraception.value: Does not reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy; use effective contraception to avoid unintended pregnancy exposure.
